report:
## Research Summary

The claim that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 originated from a March 11, 2020 letter in *The Lancet Respiratory Medicine* hypothesizing that ACE2-upregulating drugs (including some NSAIDs) could theoretically increase infection severity. This prompted French Health Minister Olivier Véran to publicly urge avoiding ibuprofen (NYT, https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/17/health/coronavirus-ibuprofen.html), and briefly the WHO echoed caution.

However, this warning was quickly retracted. Within days, WHO reversed its position, stating: "Based on currently available information, WHO does not recommend against the use of ibuprofen" (ScienceAlert, https://www.sciencealert.com/who-recommends-to-avoid-taking-ibuprofen-for-covid-19-symptoms). The European Medicines Agency similarly concluded there was "no scientific evidence establishing a link between ibuprofen and worsening of COVID-19" (EMA, https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/ema-gives-advice-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatories-covid-19), a position the FDA also supported.

Subsequent peer-reviewed research reinforced this reversal. A large 38-center hospital study and a Cochrane-style systematic review found NSAID use was **not** associated with increased COVID-19 severity, mortality, ventilation needs, or kidney injury—one large study even found NSAID use associated with *lower* mortality and severity among hospitalized patients (PMC, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9107579/; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8426976/).

**Conclusion:** The evidence does not support the claim that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19. It began as an unverified hypothesis amplified by a government warning, was retracted by WHO/EMA/FDA within days, and has since been refuted by observational studies. Standard medical guidance (e.g., NHS, Mayo Clinic) permits ibuprofen use for COVID-19 symptoms like fever and pain, same as for other illnesses.
